short: Gated AV fusion for overlapped speech (M06) is standard: AV-driven fusion weights (2006) and mixture recognition with lips (2016) came first; 15.20% to 10.31% WER, no seeds; test interferers unstated.
position: The paper [@yu2020overlapped] changes processing (M06) twice: a gated audio-visual front end inside one LF-MMI recogniser for two-talker mixtures, and a hybrid LF-MMI back end on LRS2; both are standard. Audio-visual fusion weights for a competing talker [@shao2006competing] and recognition from the mixture with lip features [@chao2016speaker], which the authors cite, came first. Gating beats concatenation, 15.20% to 10.31% average WER (Table 3), with no seeds or variance, 24 against 15 TDNN-F layers (Fig. 2, inference) and no clean-test column. The lip-reading state-of-the-art claim fails: Table 1 lists Afouras et al. without their language model (49.8%); with it they report 48.3% [@afouras2018deep] against 48.86% here. The test-interferer source and mixture count are unstated, unlike three earlier mixture studies (M12, behind); [later] work reaches 6.4% WER at -5 dB on LRS2 [@nguyen2025cocktail] against 14.22% here.
